data.name: Keshto
data.gender_notes: Keshto is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Keshto is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘kesh’, which means hair. The name is believed to be a symbol of honor, glory, and power. It is mentioned in Hindu scriptures as the name of a king or a warrior. Keshto is a powerful and majestic name, suitable for a baby boy. The name Keshto carries the meaning “Honor, Glory” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Keshto usually hope their child will grow to embody honor, glory and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Keshto belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Honor, Glory.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Keshto total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

vedic_reference.note: The name Keshto is derived from the Sanskrit word Kesha, which is the name of the demon king slain by Lord Vishnu in his incarnation as Krishna.

historical_references.reference: According to the Mahabharata, Keshto was a brahmin sage who lived during the Mahabharata war era. He was a disciple of sage Vyasa and was known for his great knowledge and wisdom. During the war, Keshto was approached by Arjuna seeking his guidance and blessings. Keshto recognized Arjuna's divine form as the avatar of Lord Vishnu and blessed him with the passage to the divine realm of Indra after his death.

Keshto was also a king who ruled over the ancient Indian kingdom of Kalinga between the 3rd and 2nd century BCE. He was known for his justice and fair rule, and is mentioned in the Jataka tales as having provided refuge to the Buddha during his wanderings in India.
